transcript:
This message comes from Odoo.
Running a business shouldn't feel like surviving a software group project.
Start managing your business with one unified system.
Odoo is the all-in-one business management software.
Try for free today at odoo.com/nprpodcasts.
Ukraine should find a new leader.
As NPR's Bill Chappell reports, Trump spoke after Volodymyr Zelensky criticized Trump's
plan to buy diesel from Russia.
On Friday night, President Zelensky said President Trump's deal to buy diesel will fuel Russia's
war effort against Ukraine.
Trump fired back at Zelensky on Saturday, saying of Ukraine, "I suggest they get a new leader
who can make a deal."
Zelensky wasn't the only person to be stunned when Trump said the U.S. would buy diesel
from Russia.
Just a few weeks ago, Trump signed a broad sanctions law against Russia.
One of its goals was to clamp down on the country's energy revenue.
The new diesel deal is seen as an attempt to ease high U.S. fuel costs, with midterm
elections looming next month.
Bill Chappell, NPR News.
While cleanup continues in Alabama and the Florida Panhandle, other parts of the Gulf
Coast are quickly returning to normal after Hurricane Isaias passed by Elise Katrin Greg
of the Gulf State newsrooms and Mississippi Public Broadcasting reports from the coasts.
After Hurricane Isaias made landfall near Destin, Florida, Mississippi's coast has been
fairly serene.
Some roads were impassable on Friday night, but had been cleared by Saturday morning.
Coastal flood advisories were in place for much of the weekend.
Thousands of people are in town for crews in the coast, a week-long event that includes
car shows and auctions.
Susan Tisdale made the 10-hour trip from South Carolina, getting in on Thursday night.
She says Friday was pretty quiet.
It was windy, but other than that, we've got very little rain or anything.
Back at home, we're getting lots of rain and some wind, but we need it.
Emergency management officials are reporting minimal damage, with some counties already
done with cleanup.
For NPR News, I'm Elise Katrin Greg in Gulfport, Mississippi.
Hurricane Simon is expected to hit Mexico's west-central coast as early as Sunday.
The storm is now a Category 4 hurricane, with sustained winds reaching as high as 150 miles
an hour.
Forecasters say Simon will unleash 10 to 20 inches of rain in many areas, with some locations
receiving as much as 30 inches of rain.
Life-threatening flooding and landslides are expected in some areas, particularly in areas
with steep landscapes.
Police in Erie, Pennsylvania, are investigating a mass shooting late Saturday night that killed
eight people after a gunman opened fire at a local residence.
Authorities say the shooter is also dead.
Erie Police Chief Rick Laura described what officers discovered.
This is one of the most difficult and heartbreaking scenes our officers and investigators have
ever encountered.
The loss of life is devastating, and the circumstances we are working through are deeply disturbing.
At this time, we can confirm that the suspect is deceased.
Based on the information currently available to us, there is no ongoing threat to the public.
So far, there has been no motive for the shooting.
You're listening to NPR News.
Christa Pike, who survived a botched execution in Tennessee, has been discharged from the
hospital and is back in prison.
NPR's Shonda Lee Stuster has more.
Attorneys for death row inmate Christa Pike said Saturday that she has been discharged
from a hospital and returned to Deborah K. Johnson Rehabilitation Center in Tennessee.
Pike had been hospitalized after she received and survived two lethal doses of the sedative
pentobarbital.
Her attorneys said in a statement that she is receiving medical care at the prison and
that they are tracking her recovery.
The statement said Pike is "grateful to the first responders and her medical team for
their care in these extraordinary circumstances."
Shonda Lee Stuster, NPR News.
Pope Leo XIV has declared capital punishment inadmissible, responding to plans by the U.S.
to live stream an execution by firing squad.
He quoted the church's position on capital punishment, saying that the death penalty
attacks the "inherent dignity of a human being."
Nidal Malik Hassan is scheduled to be executed at Fort Hood on December 3rd.
He was convicted of killing 13 people and wounding 32 others during attack at the base.
Dwight Phillips Jr. ran for 120 yards as No. 2 Georgia slipped past No. 6 Alabama Saturday
night 20-17 Gunnar Stockton accounted for both of Georgia's touchdowns.
Texas quarterback Arch Manning threw two interceptions as the No. 1 Longhorns fell to unranked Oklahoma
27-24, No. 3 Notre Dame beat Stanford 58-7 while No. 5 Ohio State beat Maryland 45-16
and Puget Sound beat Pacific Lutheran 23-13.
I'm Dale Willman, NPR News.
This message comes from Charles Schwab with their original podcast, Choiceology, hosted
by Katie Milkman, an award-winning behavioral scientist and author of the bestselling book
How to Change.
Choiceology is a show about the psychology and economics behind people's decisions.
Hear true stories from Nobel laureates, historians, authors, athletes, and more about how to make
better decisions to help avoid costly mistakes.
Download the latest episode and subscribe at Schwab.com/podcast or wherever you listen.
